input: When the selectivity values reported by the two groups are compared, a considerable discrepancy emerges, and it is instructive to consider the test conditions under which each set of values was obtained. The first group measured single-component isotherms on the benchmark material under dry, pure-gas conditions and evaluated the mixture selectivity through IAST, an approach that effectively predicts how the adsorbed phase would behave if the mixture behaved in the same way as the pure components predict. The second group, by contrast, carried out breakthrough measurements on humidified mixed feeds, in which water vapour competes for the same adsorption sites, a factor that tends to depress the measured selectivity. It is therefore not entirely surprising that the two sets of values differ, since the underlying measurements were made under markedly different conditions. Arguably, the relative weight that should be attached to each set depends on the duty for which the material is being considered: for a dried feed at low loading, the conditions are closer to those of the first group, whereas for the feed as it leaves the upstream process, humid and mixed, the conditions are closer to those of the second. On that basis, and specifically for the untreated-feed condition, a limited preference is expressed here for the second group's values, with the benchmark material ranked accordingly. It should nevertheless be noted that this preference does not extend to dried duties, nor does it resolve the behaviour of the material at water loadings beyond those explored by either group, an area in which the ranking of the benchmark material against alternative materials remains an open question.
target: Set against the values obtained on the benchmark material under dry, pure-gas conditions are the values from the second group, measured on humidified mixed feeds. The disagreement between the two sets is not a disagreement about the material. The first set comes from single-component isotherms evaluated through IAST, a route that returns the selectivity the adsorbed phase would show if the mixture behaved as the pure components predict. The second set comes from breakthrough measurements on the mixture itself, where water vapour competes for the same sites and the measured selectivity falls. Which set deserves more weight depends on the duty the material is being selected for. A separation run on a dried feed, at low loading, sits close to the conditions of the first set, and there the higher values are the relevant ones. A separation run on the feed as it leaves the upstream process, humid and mixed, sits close to the second. On that condition — the feed untreated, the water present — the preference here rests with the second group's values, and the benchmark material is ranked on those values rather than on the higher dry figures. The preference is limited to that condition. It does not extend to dried duties, and it does not settle how the material behaves once the water loading rises beyond what either group tested, a range in which neither set of measurements was taken and in which the ranking of the benchmark material against its rivals remains open.
